terms.gloss: a person, a human being (man or woman)
evidence: Cic. Fin. 1.13: homō omnī doctrīnā ērudītus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Homō is a person of either sex; the plural hominēs is “people”. Persōna is a mask or a role, and so a person seen in a part or a standing (mea persōna, Cic. Att. 8.11D.7, Lewis & Short), or a party at law; for a human being as such the word is homō.

sources: Lewis & Short: homo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 359.
